stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Which expression is equivalent to 5·2^(3x−1)?

rationales.B: 10·8^x treats 2^(−1) as 2, multiplying by 2 instead of dividing by 2: 5·2·8^x = 10·8^x. Check at x = 1: it gives 80, not 20.
rationales.C: 5·6^(x−1) multiplies the base 2 by the coefficient 3 of x to get 6 and keeps the −1 in the exponent. Check at x = 1: it gives 5·6⁰ = 5, not 20. The factor 2^(3x) is (2³)^x = 8^x, not 6^x.
rationales.D: (5/2)·6^x handles the −1 correctly (the factor 1/2) but replaces 2³ with 2·3 = 6, so 2^(3x) becomes 6^x instead of 8^x. Check at x = 1: it gives 15, not 20.

stem: A data set shows output values whose ratios between consecutive equal-interval inputs are all approximately 1.2 (the small differences come from rounding). A student instead runs an exponential regression on a calculator and obtains an r-squared value of 0.999, citing this as justification that the data is exponential. Is this reasoning valid for determining the appropriate model type?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No -- the constant ratio itself is what establishes an exponential model; a high r-squared value alone is not sufficient justification

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes -- a high r-squared value is sufficient to justify any regression model type

choices.label: C
choices.text: No -- only a perfect r-squared of 1 would justify the model

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, but only if r-squared is reported to at least four decimal places

rationales.A: Per documented AP scoring guidance, citing a regression fit statistic instead of computing the actual ratio of consecutive outputs is explicitly insufficient reasoning, even when the classification is correct.
rationales.B: A high r-squared value describes fit quality, not the underlying structural pattern (constant ratio) that defines an exponential model.
rationales.C: This still relies on the regression statistic rather than the required ratio-based reasoning.
rationales.D: The precision of the reported statistic does not change that it is not valid justification for the model type.

stem: Which expression is equivalent to log base 5 of (25x^3)?

rationales.A: log_5(25x^3) = log_5(25) + log_5(x^3) = 2 + 3*log_5(x), since 5^2 = 25 (product property, then power property).
rationales.B: 6*log_5(x) comes from multiplying the constant 2 (the value of log_5(25)) by the exponent 3 instead of adding. The product property turns 25x^3 into a sum, log_5(25) + log_5(x^3) = 2 + 3*log_5(x). Check at x = 5: log_5(25*125) = 5, but 6*log_5(5) = 6.
rationales.C: 3*log_5(25x) = 3*(2 + log_5(x)) = 6 + 3*log_5(x) applies the exponent 3 to the whole argument, as if the expression were (25x)^3. The 3 is the exponent of x only. Check at x = 5: this gives 9, not 5.
rationales.D: 5 + 3*log_5(x) takes log_5(25) to be 5 instead of 2 (5^2 = 25, so the logarithm is 2). Check at x = 5: this gives 8, not 5.
